1 غَتِمَ , aor.
غَتَمَ , inf. n. غَتَمٌ, He had an impotence, or an impediment, or a difficulty, in his
speech, or utterance; and a barbarousness, or vitiousness, therein, especially in speaking Arabic; i. e., a want of clearness, perspicuousness, distinctness, chasteness, or correctness, therein. (Msb.) ＝
-A2- غَتَمَ, said of food (طَعَام), It was, or became, wholesome, or beneficial. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
